correctness.rationale: The strict metric domain, polarity and zero-sum Euclidean normalization are explicit. The connected tight-edge criterion yields an exhaustive vertex classification. Centered squared norms are given by an exact completed-square identity, proving radius and all tangent-facet counts. Opposite tangent facets and blockwise permutation spans prove that maximal-ball center dimension is exactly 0 or 1 with the stated parity/resonance conditions. Six independent halfspace-intersection finite checks and nine further exact rational tests passed; these are not substituted for infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The closest published result enumerates all interior dual vertices but does not evaluate Euclidean facet distances, optimal-center affine dimensions, or exact rational resonances. The existing complete-multipartite Euclidean inradius formulas apply only at the unit-edge graph metric endpoint t=2, not to the strict snowflake interpolation. The new parity-dependent center rigidity does not follow as a named assertion from those works without the independent squared-normal optimization and tangent span analysis. Targeted database and primary literature comparisons located no exact equivalent; bibliographic uncertainty remains.

value.rationale: The snowflake deformation is a natural interpolation of complete bipartite graph metrics whose number of dual vertices is constant throughout the interval. Nonetheless Euclidean maximum-ball centers exhibit a sharp parity- and arithmetic-dependent uniqueness transition; the theorem provides every radius, tangent facet count and optimal-center affine dimension, including explicit rational resonances. This supplies new structural metric information rather than another aggregate facet enumeration.
